requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate. They cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items` that is assessed here.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**
- **Block mapping entries are `pair` items named by the written key.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys]` parses `a: 1` and `"b":`, and asserts the selectors `pair[a]` and `pair["b"]`. The quoted key keeps its written form, quotes included.
- **Flow mapping entries are `pair` items.** The same test parses `c: {d: 1}` and asserts `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d]`.
- **Block sequence entries are anonymous `item` nodes.** The same test parses `- f: 1` and `- 2` under `e:`, and asserts `item@` selectors with their spans. A sequence entry that holds a mapping is covered (`item@/pair[f]`). A scalar sequence entry is covered too.
- **Nested entries appear beneath the nearest enclosing item.** The summary strings show full parent/child paths such as `pair["b"]/pair[e]/item@/pair[f]`. The line spans (1-2, 3-7, 4-4, 5-7, 6-6, 7-7) are asserted as well.
- **Selected source ends at the last non-comment token.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[yaml_selection_ends_before_trailing_comment_tokens]` makes three assertions.
  - `key: value # trailing comment` selects as `key: value`.
  - The item span is exactly `Span::new(0, 10)`.
  - For a nested mapping followed by a comment line, `pair[a]` selects `a:\n  b: 1` without the comment before `d`. `pair[a]/pair[b]` selects `b: 1`.
- **Comment ownership under `requirements.references.outline_comments`.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` asserts that a comment before `second:` belongs to `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`, not to the previous key. This requirement is cited rather than owned here, and the general comment-run rules have their own tests.
- **Selector syntax, percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate suffixes.** These are cited from `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, so they need no test here.

**Negative cases and other gaps considered**
- A flow sequence is not a block sequence entry. An unmarked test, `outline_content.rs#fn[language_name_spans_retain_original_bytes_when_selectors_are_normalized]`, covers `key: [1]`. Its expected names list contains only `key`. That is a marking issue at most, not an assertion gap.
- A top-level block sequence is exercised in `#fn[no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds]`.
- I found no distinct input class in the requirement that these tests miss.

All asserted outcomes agree with the requirement text.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
